Promotion resolves every identifier a manifest cites against the repository and refuses one resolving to no object; merged at e147cbed, verified in HEAD by the markers the change introduced rather than by reachability. Gate: the node's own file is 10 passed exit 0 at the delivered tree; the wider population is 1 failed 136 passed at head against the identical failure id and count at base aecb4e5f, so no failure is added; the declared mutation reddens exactly the three refusal cases at 3 failed 7 passed with the declaration verbatim on the red log's first line. Independent review 86/100 (durability 16, evidence 15, fit 18, goal fidelity 18, scope discipline 19), three findings all carried. Two the coordinator found independently: the manifest cited four gate logs under the configuration home where none existed while the real logs sit under the checkout's reports root, a cited identifier resolving to no store and so this section's own defect committed by its own record; and no gate log's first line names the revision, tree or command that the template this plan landed requires. The third is the reviewer's and is the substantive one: the case at tests/test_cited_identifier_resolves.py:369 passes under the declared mutation because a fabricated citation left unrefused still trips the worktree-head guard, so its assertion holds whichever refusal fired and would not catch a regression. A fourth, found while assembling this citation: gate-head-new-file.log is misnamed, carrying the population plus the new file at 1 failed 138 passed rather than the file alone, so the manifest's ten-passed claim was backed only by the post-revert control log. The test_logs citation is repaired to the four paths that exist, each verified by read-back, with the delivered manifest kept as manifest.md.asdelivered so a repaired field stays distinguishable from a fabricated one.

reckon-ship · 2026-09-23T01:07:10.790Z

The independent review of the citation-resolution node, dispatched under a fresh node id after the first reviewer died in the provider usage-limit window. It scored 86 across five dimensions and produced three findings, all carried into the successor followup. Two it reached independently of the coordinator, which had found them separately and deliberately withheld them: the manifest cited four gate logs at a root where none existed, and no gate log's first line names the revision, tree or command the template requires. The third is the review's alone and is the substantive one: a case that passes under the declared mutation because an unrefused citation still trips a later guard, so its assertion cannot separate the two and would not catch a regression. Convergence from an uninformed reviewer on the first two is what makes the third worth acting on. Recorded separately because this promotion demonstrated the guard the reviewed node landed: this run's own manifest wrote commits as prose, the one-line list field split it on a comma, and a sentence fragment was offered to the ledger as a commit. The new check resolved it, found no object, and refused — hours after the code shipped, against the coordinator promoting it. Before today that fragment would have been recorded as a citation nobody could ever follow.

§19 — A gate population names files the repository has

reckon-ship · 2026-09-22T16:15:00+02:00

Gate passed: seven cases, the declared mutation reddening exactly the two refusal cases while the five negative halves stayed green (2 failed, 5 passed, exit 1), which is what separates a mutation that reddens the refusal from one that breaks something else. Three of the seven are the worker's own additions and one of them makes the check safe to have at all: a population the node declares it will WRITE is admitted, without which this refusal would reject nearly every node shipped on this plan, since each gates on a test file it is about to create. The other two are false-positive guards — a literal path matching no file is not a population, and a ratio in a measure is not read as a path. Review 86/100 with evidence 12, for a red log that paraphrases the declared mutation while the evidence anchor claimed it repeated it verbatim. The anchor is corrected at HEAD and the promotion carries a waiver; the declaration was not edited to match, because a check satisfiable by rewriting its own input measures nothing. Third such waiver on this plan, all three a worker wording a mutation differently from the coordinator, none catching an unsound control — which is the evidence the lead's write-time decision rests on.

# Read-back — §20 "A control is judged by what it did, not by how it was worded"

Node: `second-read-back-of-the-control-gate-section` — plan `reckon:crew-runtime-positive-controls` §20, role review.
Base revision: `2014c4801f6f04c36684bef91c7d83e79b1b6e60`, worktree `/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/.reckon-worktrees/reckon-c8f839407e49/ship-crpc-20260921/second-read-back-of-the-control-gate-section`.
Section read: `docs/plans/crew-runtime-positive-controls.html`, lines 1066–1099 at that revision — the section as authored, before any implementing node has been dispatched against it.

This document restates §20's intent and its done-when in other words; it lists the section's sentences that carry more than one reading, quoting each and giving both readings; and for each of the five case clauses in the done-when paragraph it names one observation that would satisfy the case and one that would not. It neither proposes the change nor opposes it, and it takes no position on whether the change is made.

## 1. The section, in other words

**The present state it describes.** A node whose declared write paths include a test file carries a negative-control declaration: the mutation its added tests must fail against. The worker applies that mutation, watches the tests redden, and records the red log beside the run's manifest. The admission test under discussion decides whether that control's evidence is acceptable, and it works on wording: it looks for the declaration's text inside the red log's own text.

**The two failings it reports.** First, across the plan and the sprint behind the recorded decision, twelve controls that had genuinely been exercised were turned away by that wording test, while the test has never once turned away a control that had not been exercised. The refusals clustered in the field's shape: workers wrote the log's location followed by an explanation, a structure of named sub-keys, a heading with the path beneath, a relative path with a label — each a fair reading of a field called a log, each carrying more than the guard wanted, each refused. Second, the test is satisfiable without evidence: pasting the declaration into the log passes it, and nothing in the record tells that apart from an honest red run.

**What it asks for.** The admission test moves onto two facts about the control run itself: its exit status is not zero, and the set of tests it failed is not the same as the baseline's. The declaration is not dropped; it stays where the dispatch already puts it, on the node record, and is shown together with the log's location at promotion so that a person, rather than a string comparison, judges whether the mutation matches. The section places this beside the two sections before it: consult what the store recorded rather than judge the form of the sentence describing it.

**What it asks to be tested.** One new file, `tests/test_control_gate_checks_facts.py`, with five case clauses: (1) a control whose run exited non-zero with a failure set differing from the baseline's is admitted whatever its wording reads, including a declaration sharing no word with its log; (2) a control whose run exited zero is refused; (3) a control that exited non-zero while failing exactly the baseline's set is refused, the case a wording test cannot detect at all; (4) a green run whose log's first line only restates the declaration is refused, closing the round trip the old guard allowed; (5) the promotion's output carries the declaration's text next to the log's path, so the human comparison the decision leans on genuinely appears. The paragraph closes with the standing record convention: apply the declared mutation, watch the new file fail, and record the red log whose first line carries the mutation verbatim.

**What it explicitly leaves out.** It owns one property — what the guard judges — and four record repairs found nearby travel in the followup instead of being folded in: a test case that must name which guard fired, a gate log that must carry its revision on line one, a log whose name must match its contents, and a presented citation that must be refused rather than filtered.

## 2. Sentences carrying more than one reading

Each span below is quoted from the section (markup stripped, whitespace collapsed; the read-back gate re-checks every quote against the section source at the base revision). Both readings are given, with the difference each makes. The done-when's second clause — a control whose run exits zero is refused — carries no entry here: every part of it reads one way.

### 2.1 — the admission sentence

> The declared negative control is admitted by comparing the declaration against the text of the red log.

- Reading (a): the compared text is the red-log entry as written, in full, so the declaration's string anywhere inside it qualifies.
- Reading (b): the comparison reads that entry's first line only, so a declaration on a second line does not qualify however plainly it is stated.
- What differs: under (b) a two-line entry — a path on line one, the declaration on line two — is refused even with the declaration present; under (a) it qualifies on its text alone.

### 2.2 — the five shapes

> Five workers produced five shapes — a path followed by an em dash and prose, a mapping of sub-keys, a markdown heading with the path beneath, a relative path with a labelled second line — every one a reasonable reading of a field whose name says log, every one carrying at least as much information as the guard wanted, every one refused.

- Reading (a): five distinct shapes, of which the list names four — one shape's description is absent from this sentence.
- Reading (b): five counts the produced entries and the four items are the distinct shapes, one of them produced twice — the decision record behind the section carries exactly that note, path-plus-em-dash-and-prose "(twice, already recorded)" — so the list is complete and the count is the arithmetic.
- What differs: whether a reader of the read-back holds the full inventory here or must find the fifth entry in the record to reconstruct the population.

### 2.3 — the defeat and the person it blocks

> The comparison is also defeatable in the one direction that matters, by the person it blocks

- Pair 1 — > the one direction that matters:
  - Reading (a): the direction that matters is a false admission — an unexercised control passing the guard — and the person it blocks is the node whose promotion waits on evidence.
  - Reading (b): the direction that matters is the false refusal — sound controls turned away, twelve of them — and the person it blocks is the worker whose honest control was refused and who pastes the declaration to get through.
  - What differs: who the blocked person is, and whether the pasting is the scene's villain or its casualty.
- Pair 2 — > nothing afterwards distinguishes that from an honest re-run:
  - Reading (a): nothing in the record consulted at admission distinguishes the two — the record's silence after the guard passed.
  - Reading (b): nothing anywhere distinguishes the two, for any later reader — a claim about the world, not about the record.
  - What differs: under (b) the sentence asserts an undetectability no later inspection could lift; under (a) it asserts only that the record as read at admission carries no such distinction.

### 2.4 — the replacement sentence

> Replace it with the two facts a guard can verify without reading any wording: the control run exits non-zero, and its failure set differs from the baseline's.

- Pair 1 — > its failure set differs from the baseline's:
  - Reading (a): any inequality admits — a failure set that is a strict subset of the baseline's (a pre-existing failure gone, none added) also counts as differing.
  - Reading (b): admission needs at least one failure the baseline does not carry; a subset then fails the second fact and is refused by the guard's default.
  - What differs: which way the subset shape falls — no case clause names it, so this pair decides it.
- Pair 2 — > the two facts a guard can verify without reading any wording:
  - Reading (a): the guard reads the control run's own machine output — its exit status and the failing-test names its runner printed, in the log the declaration points at.
  - Reading (b): the guard reads fields on the node record, and no run output is opened at all.
  - What differs: whether a declared log location that resolves to nothing is itself a refusal — under (a) the facts cannot be read, under (b) the file was never needed.

### 2.5 — the declaration and its display

> Keep the declaration where it already lives on the node record, and print it beside the log in the promotion output so a person judges the match.

- Pair 1 — > the promotion output:
  - Reading (a): the text the promotion command prints as it runs — the coordinator's terminal.
  - Reading (b): the record the promotion writes — the row's own text a later reader opens.
  - What differs: which surface an asserting test or checker reads, and where the person judging the pair must look.
- Pair 2 — > print it beside the log:
  - Reading (a): beside the log's path — the location stated next to the declaration.
  - Reading (b): beside the log's contents — the log's own text placed next to the declaration.
  - What differs: whether the implementing node emits the log's text or only where it sits; the fifth case clause's phrase "beside the log path" reads this one way.

### 2.6 — the first case clause

> a control whose run exits non-zero with a failure set differing from the baseline's is admitted whatever its wording, including a declaration sharing no words with its log

- Pair — > including a declaration sharing no words with its log:
  - Reading (a): no property of the log's text constrains admission, and the fixture's log may hold anything.
  - Reading (b): no wording constrains admission, but the log the declaration points at is still opened, so its location must resolve; a fixture whose declared log was never written then fails this clause rather than passing it.
  - What differs: whether the fixture writes the file at all, and whether a declared-but-absent log is a shape this clause covers or no clause does.

### 2.7 — the third case clause

> a control exiting non-zero with a failure set identical to the baseline's is refused, which is the case a substring test cannot see at all

- Pair — > identical to the baseline's:
  - Reading (a): identical means equal as sets, so its complement "differing" in the first clause means any inequality, which admits the strict subset.
  - Reading (b): identical is the tight wording for a looser fact — no failure beyond the baseline's was added — with "differing" then meaning at least one new failure, and equal and subset both refused.
  - What differs: the subset shape again, and whether this clause's refusal covers it directly or the guard's default does.

### 2.8 — the fourth case clause

> a log whose first line merely repeats the declaration while the run exited zero is refused, which is the defeat the old guard admitted

- Pair — the source of the refusal:
  - Reading (a): the refusal falls out of the exit-status fact alone; the fixture pins the old defeat closed by reproducing it.
  - Reading (b): the repetition in the first line is itself part of the refusal, so a first-line comparison survives into the gate.
  - What differs: under (b) the implementing node writes a check that reads the log's first line; under (a) no check reads the log's text at all.

### 2.9 — the fifth case clause

> the promotion output carries the declaration text beside the log path so the human comparison the decision relies on is actually available

- Pair — > the promotion output:
  - Reading (a): printed on promotion — "available" means on screen at the moment of promotion.
  - Reading (b): stored in the record promotion writes — "available" means retrievable afterwards from the record.
  - What differs: when the person judging the pair must be present for the comparison to be possible, and which artifact a test asserts on this clause by.

### 2.10 — the recording convention

> The declared mutation is applied, tests/test_control_gate_checks_facts.py is observed to fail, and the red log is recorded with the mutation verbatim on its first line.

- Pair 1 — > with the mutation verbatim on its first line:
  - Reading (a): the declared text appears verbatim within the first line — a labelled line, a prefix followed by the text, qualifies.
  - Reading (b): the first line is exactly the declared text and nothing else.
  - What differs: a fleet whose recorded logs conventionally carry a label on that line passes this arm under (a) and fails under (b).
- Pair 2 — who reads that line:
  - Reading (a): the convention governs the node's own record-keeping, and no check in the new gate reads the log's text.
  - Reading (b): the gate itself checks the first line, putting a wording test back on a surface whose wording test the section removes.
  - What differs: whether the implementing node builds a first-line check into the gate or only follows the convention.

## 3. The five done-when cases

The done-when clauses are quoted in their order; each is followed by one observation that would satisfy the clause and one that would not. An observation is a fixture together with the admission choice it produces at promotion, where the guard lives.

### Case 1 — admission follows what the run did

> a control whose run exits non-zero with a failure set differing from the baseline's is admitted whatever its wording, including a declaration sharing no words with its log

- **An observation that would satisfy it:** a control whose recorded run exited non-zero while failing at least one test the baseline does not, its declaration worded so that no word of it appears in the log's text — promotion admits the control and the run proceeds.
- **An observation that would not satisfy it:** the same facts — non-zero exit, one added failure, unrelated wording — with promotion refusing the control.

One variant sits at this clause's edge, decided by 2.6: an added failure present while the declared log location resolves to nothing at all. The clause as worded holds on the run's facts alone.

### Case 2 — a green run is refused

> a control whose run exits zero is refused

- **An observation that would satisfy it:** a control whose recorded run exited zero — a green run, declaration present on the node record — with promotion refusing the control and admitting nothing.
- **An observation that would not satisfy it:** that same green control admitted.

### Case 3 — the case a wording test cannot see

> a control exiting non-zero with a failure set identical to the baseline's is refused, which is the case a substring test cannot see at all

- **An observation that would satisfy it:** a control whose recorded run exited non-zero while failing exactly the set the baseline already fails, its declaration restated word-for-word as the log's first line — promotion refuses the control.
- **An observation that would not satisfy it:** the same fixture admitted — a non-zero control failing only the pre-existing set passing the gate.

Under the comparison as it stands this same fixture is admitted, the declaration's text sitting inside the log's text — which is the shape the clause calls the case a substring test cannot see at all. One further shape sits between this clause and the first: a control whose failure set is a strict subset of the baseline's, a pre-existing failure gone with none added. No clause words it, and 2.4's first pair decides which way it falls.

### Case 4 — the pasted declaration no longer buys admission

> a log whose first line merely repeats the declaration while the run exited zero is refused, which is the defeat the old guard admitted

- **An observation that would satisfy it:** a control whose recorded run exited zero while its log's first line is the declaration's own text — promotion refuses, where the old comparison admitted the same shape.
- **An observation that would not satisfy it:** that fixture admitted — a green run whose log simply restates the declaration passing the gate, which is the defeat this clause closes.

Whether the refusal rests on the run's exit alone or on a first-line rule surviving into the new gate is 2.8's pair; the clause's own "while the run exited zero" is what carries it.

### Case 5 — the pair is on show

> the promotion output carries the declaration text beside the log path so the human comparison the decision relies on is actually available

- **An observation that would satisfy it:** a completed promotion whose output shows the declaration's text and the log's declared path in the same view — printed, or stored in the record promotion writes, per 2.9's pair — so the comparison needs no second lookup.
- **An observation that would not satisfy it:** either half missing from that one view — the path shown without the declaration text, or the declaration reachable only from the node record.

2.9's pair decides which surface counts as the promotion's output here, and 2.5's first pair carries the same question for the paragraph's own sentence.

§34 — A reclaimed run's review keys on its own head

reckon-build · 2026-10-03T00:39:08.591Z

In reckon/crew/recovery.py, _record_carried_head resolves an abbreviated commits: entry of seven or more hex characters to its full object id through the run's repository (rev-parse --verify with the commit peel appended), skipping an entry resolved neither way; a reclaimed run's review head is read from its own record instead of the shared checkout's HEAD, and the empty head accepts no stored record (select_review_for_head), so the compose path refuses with a reason naming the missing head and the carry-forward head move (review_head_move, through _run_head_for_review) resolves the same head rather than the checkout's; the case pinning the superseded fallback was updated to this reading under a coordinator scope decision, its first assertion kept and its second replaced with an empty head accepting no record and composing no review. Arm of record at 2b8f0e7a4: base 168 passed EXIT=0, head 170 passed, 1 skipped, EXIT=0, no added failure id; negative control with the abbreviation resolution removed reds the nine-character case, 1 failed 1 passed, EXIT=1; landing record docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/reclaimed-run-review-keys-on-its-own-head.html.

reckon-build · 2026-10-03T01:25:13.727Z

Stored a parsed five-dimension review of run r-20261002T222352532588-reclaimed-run-review-keys-on-its-own-head (base 18d9e07b0, head 44d0e8c1c) at both granted store paths; total 85 (goal_fidelity 17, evidence 16, scope_discipline 19, durability 15, fit 18), added_failure_count 0 with no ids derived from the reviewed run's own baseline_suite and after_suite gate logs; one follow-on finding — two readers (reckon/cli.py:4753 and reckon/crew/obligations.py:592) still call _reviewed_run_head directly and resolve the shared checkout's HEAD for a reclaimed run, contradicting §34's absolute clause.

The reading for a run whose record resolves no head now lives in one function, newest_review_for_headless_run: a reclaimed worktree is still refused, and every other headless record reads the store's newest record, so the obligations duty reader again produces a live run's sub-floor disposition duty instead of skipping it over a head the pointer cannot resolve. reckon-build · 2026-10-03T09:24:05.594Z

An empty or unreadable node claim is given a 5-second grace period for its writer to land and is then reclaimed exactly as a dead holder's claim is, so a dispatcher killed between the exclusive create and its record write no longer wedges the node, and a pid beyond the kernel's int range now refuses under D12 instead of raising OverflowError out of the dispatch; eight cases in tests/test_concurrent_dispatch_of_one_node.py pass at head against the base arm's two failing new cases, ruff adds no finding, and the declared mutation reddens the fresh-empty case with 1 failed EXIT=1, while the record is blocked on one head-arm failure id the base arm did not carry and the evidence that it does not come from these commits is in the fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/node-claim-survives-a-corrupt-record.html

promotion release clears the arms, basetemps and control trees a manifest declares in its structured fields, removes them only under the node-local temp root and only when the gate passed, copies their declared logs into the run directory first, and records removals, kept paths and copied logs on the release mapping; reckon/crew/promotion.py

s22-coord · 2026-10-04T16:45:00Z

Landed at merge 569b07121. Promotion of a run whose gate passed removes the arms, basetemps and control trees its manifest declares in the structured fields that carry them: test_logs, negative_control_log, the suite records' log and --basetemp, and the declared paths of artifacts. It copies their declared logs into the run directory first, and records removals, kept paths and copies on the release. Removal stays within the node-local temp root and skips any path another live run cites. The coordinator sent the worker back twice for safety. First, the initial head treated any absolute path in the manifest's prose as an owned arm, and it cleared arms on failed and blocked gates too. Second, the corrected head still read artifacts descriptions rather than their declared path keys. Measured at a stacked merge of main 0513a121e over 60 importer files: 530 passed at both arms. That population missed the new test file, which imports reckon.crew, so a focused gate at the merged head covered it: 80 passed, exit 0. Reviews scored 93 and 94. reckon-f7's orphan-scratch sweep and /tmp-headroom refusal (4c86e0ccf) are the backstop.

§58 — The reap test asks only about the children it launched

reckon-build · 2026-10-04T19:53:56.645Z

Landed on tests/test_resume_reaps_its_child.py at 9d486d3db: _no_defunct_launched_child waits on each pid the case launched instead of os.waitpid(-1), so an exited, unreaped child another case on the same xdist worker left behind is neither reaped nor reported; the new paired case leaves such a corpse of its own in the process and the reap case beside it still passes (gate: 20 of 20 runs green at -n 8, 6 passed each); the defunct-launcher control arm reddens the four reap cases (4 failed, 2 passed); restoring waitpid(-1) in the helper reddens the paired case (1 failed, 5 passed, EXIT=1)

s22-coord · 2026-10-04T20:02:00Z

Landed at merge a4ab6afb2. _no_defunct_launched_child waits on each pid the case launched with os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG), so an exited child that another case on the same xdist worker left behind is neither reaped nor reported. test_an_unreaped_child_of_this_process_does_not_redden_the_reap_case holds such a child of its own and the reap case beside it still passes. The file passed 20 of 20 runs at -n 8. Restoring waitpid(-1) reddens the paired case, and a launcher that leaves its worker defunct still reddens the four reap cases. Review scored 92 with no added failures. Its follow-on is §59.

strict-arms-refusal-impact — delivered report

Cited from /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/s22-coord/strict-arms-refusal-impact/report.md.

# What the unmerged baseline-arm completion rule does to real promotions

**Node:** `strict-arms-refusal-impact` · run `r-20260929T151851526457`
**Candidate repair:** `09d4deea12b86a52a2e454053a0ffce8a8685917` (over `7e452839`,
run `r-20260929T145500577980`) — `_baseline_suite_failure_ids` returns `None`
when an arm omits `completed` or carries null, and the control is refused when
neither arm is readable.
**Main arm:** `d0f0c9ab9c90dca0558682b306f651b43d5ab87b`.

`reckon/crew/promotion.py` is byte-identical between the assigned worktree HEAD
(`1af8e33f`) and `main` (`d0f0c9ab`); the only diff on `main` is an unrelated
test file. The two trees differ only by the repair, confirmed by module sha256
(`6d19f6b249d09edd48c2fbe9963f8bcbf2a6cef149267b19e2fd5da4825d42d6` main
against `75fe118e3e53c15632c4e250f6f372fbcec0de9dd2afd06f4e28e65505203cd5`
repair, as the two check-log headers record).

## Verdict

| measure | figure |
|---|---|
| population | **108** runs |
| controls main admits | **82** |
| controls 09d4deea admits | **77** |
| **admitted on main, refused at 09d4deea** | **5** |
| refused on main, admitted at 09d4deea | 0 |
| control-gate test ids red at 09d4deea, green at main | **0** (43 passed both arms) |

## Population

Ledger rows under `docs/state/reckon/runs` dated 2026-09-28 or later: **334**.
Kept — manifest still on disk **and** a declared negative-control mutation:
**108**. Skipped: 222 no declaration, 3 declared `none: <reason>`, 1 manifest not
on disk.

## Completed-key counts per arm

Disjoint, over the 108 manifests as they stand on disk:

| arms declaring `completed: true` | count |
|---|---|
| both `baseline_suite` and `after_suite` | 68 |
| `baseline_suite` only | 0 |
| `after_suite` only | 1 |
| **neither** | **39** |

Marginal readings: `completed` on `baseline_suite` **68**, on `after_suite`
**69**, on neither **39**. Within the 39: `baseline_suite` recorded but not
complete in **23**, `after_suite` recorded but not complete in **23**, and
`baseline_suite` absent entirely in **16** (an absent arm reads as the empty arm
in *both* trees, so it is not at risk).

## The five controls that flip

All five have the `completed` key **present with a null value** on both arms —
not absent. Main falls back to the baseline mapping and reads it as an empty
failure set, so every failure the control names is "added"; 09d4deea finds no
readable arm and refuses.

| run id | ledger verdict | ledger guard |
|---|---|---|
| `r-20260928T061043305378-the-project-watch-test-terminates` | matched | wording |
| `r-20260928T132148906656-resumed-burn-prices-to-rollout` | matched | facts |
| `r-20260928T160825030673-typed-discovery-skips-evidence-fragments` | matched | facts |
| `r-20260929T035930031370-rearm-replays-the-fleet-with-recorded-times` | matched | facts |
| `r-20260929T073847002082-velocity-view-in-the-spa` | matched | facts |

Four of the five carry the promotion-time verdict `matched` **recorded by the
facts guard itself**, including the `added_failure_ids` the check computed then —
so these are admissions by the same rule `main` runs today, not an artifact of
reconstruction.

## Control-gate test delta

Files whose name contains `negative_control` or `control_gate` — six at both
revisions, identical lists:

`tests/test_control_gate_checks_facts.py`,
`tests/test_crew_declared_negative_control.py`,
`tests/test_crew_negative_control_header.py`,
`tests/test_crew_negative_control_interface.py`,
`tests/test_negative_control_log_is_a_path.py`,
`tests/test_negative_control_waiver.py`

**Main: 43 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. 09d4deea: 43 passed, 0 failed, exit 0.**
The delta is empty — no id is red at `09d4deea` and green at main. The named
population does not pin the new behaviour; the repair's own case file
(`tests/test_control_is_compared_with_the_head_arm.py`) does not match the
declared name filter and is therefore outside it. This is an attribution, not a
verdict: an empty delta means the population is silent on the change, it does
not mean the change is unverified by anything — `7e452839` adds its cases to
that other file.

## Positive control on the measurement instrument

A passing suite never shows a guard fires, so the same minimal manifest — both
arms recorded with `completed: null`, over a log recording `EXIT=1` and one
failing id — was put to each tree:

```
main tree   /tmp/arms-tree-main/reckon/crew/promotion.py   -> ADMITTED (matched)
repair tree /tmp/arms-tree-repair/reckon/crew/promotion.py -> REFUSED  (no readable comparison arm)
```

Each tree's `promotion.__file__` was asserted inside that tree before any call, and
the two trees carry different markers (`no readable comparison arm is recorded`:
0 on main, 1 at 09d4deea). The 5-vs-0 delta above is therefore a difference the
instrument can see, not a null result.

## Fidelity of the re-evaluation — what bounds it

Re-evaluating main over the 108 manifests reproduces the ledger's recorded
verdict exactly for **79** and differs for **29**. Both causes are named:

- **Rows promoted before §20's facts rewrite** (32 of 108 carry a
  `negative_control` row with no `control_exit_status`, written by the old
  wording guard): 13 agree, 19 differ. These runs were admitted by a rule that
  no longer exists; the comparison is not like-for-like.
- **Operator waivers** — 14 rows were waived with `--waive-negative-control`.
  This harness passes no waiver, so it refuses 8 of them where promotion
  admitted by explicit operator action.
- **Genuine manifest drift** among the 76 facts-guard rows: **2** rows
  (`matched` in the ledger, `refused` now) — **2.6 %**.

The headline count rests on promotion-time evidence for 4 of the 5 flips and is
unaffected by the drift rows, which are not among the five.

## Logs

All under `/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260929T151851526457-strict-arms-refusal-impact/logs/`:

| log | contains |
|---|---|
| `population.json` | the 108-row population and the skip counts |
| `check-main.log` / `check-main.json` | tree, revision, module sha256, per-run verdicts at main; ends `EXIT=0` |
| `check-repair.log` / `check-repair.json` | same at 09d4deea; ends `EXIT=0` |
| `comparison.json` / `comparison-console.txt` | the per-run delta and the completion census |
| `tests-main.log` / `tests-repair.log` | the six-file population per tree; each ends `EXIT=0` |
| `positive-control.log` | both trees on one manifest; ends `EXIT=0` |

## Caveats

- The manifest measured is the one on disk **now**; a run whose manifest was
  rewritten after promotion is measured as it stands.
- The baseline arm here is `baseline_suite` as declared in the manifest; the
  head arm `after_suite` decides whenever it is readable, in both trees, so the
  repair changes only the fallback path.
- No repository path was modified by this node; it is a read-only measurement.

Its central finding is that sections 2, 6 and 7 named no file at all, describing their surfaces rather than locating them, and section 3 named its decisive files only in a retrospective paragraph. unknown · 2026-09-23

Correction to a promoted outcome. The ledger row for r-20260922T213939819649-review-of-a-cited-identifier-resolves-in-its-own-store records that the run ended "during the provider usage-limit window that stopped every run in this project". That cause is wrong and is corrected here rather than edited there, so the record shows what was originally claimed.

The coordinator's own claude.ai usage limit did reset in that window, and the two were conflated. They are different lanes: the worker ran on clive against a locally served model, which an account-level limit on a different provider cannot reach. The run's stream carries zero rate-limit rejected events across 1171 records, and its one error record is a benign missing-file tool result, so nothing in its own evidence supports the stated cause.

What is established is only the timing and the shape: the process ended at 21:45:34Z, 322 s in, mid-orientation, with a complete stream and no terminal manifest, and several peer sessions' runs went terminal in the same 21:40-22:20Z window. Real turns and tool use, no error text, no deliverable is the silent-degradation signature rather than a launch failure. The cause is unestablished, and saying so is the accurate record.

This matters beyond bookkeeping. The locally served lane was cancelled outright at 06:12 the following morning by a broad job cancellation, and a peer session is restarting it. If that service was already degrading eight hours earlier, a clean restart will look like a repair while leaving the fault in place — so an unexplained death recorded as explained would have removed the only evidence pointing at it.

A correlation, unverified as a cause, holds for both deaths. In each, a follower printed the producer's runs older code … reloading itself notice and that follower then ended, and the producer stopped soon after. imas-ambix: follower Monitor expiry at 12:57:46Z, last log line 12:58:12Z, 26 s later. reckon: s22-coord's follower ended at 15:09:16Z after printing the notice (21394ffd vs 4a2d5c19), and the producer's last log line is at 15:12:38Z. Follower expiries with no reload in progress did not kill the producer, five on imas-ambix and three on reckon, including one at 16:58Z. The current reckon producer (pid 2021676) runs under a detached wrapper, ppid 1 with its own session (sid 2021667), so it is not in the follower's process group while it is not reloading. The question to settle is what the reload depends on that the ending follower takes with it. Evidence collected by imas-ambix-cb: ~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/reckon/producer-reload-evidence.md.

The control case was observed at 17:09Z. The reckon producer reloaded (630be486 to c6b94ef9) while s22-coord's follower was alive and not expiring. pid 2021676 survived with its seat descriptor intact, the events file resumed within 10 s, and the published snapshot carries the new code stamp. A second instance, reported by imas-ambix-cb. That producer (pid 2036256) completed a reload at 19:30:30Z, logging started its reload; awaiting replacement and then completed its reload; publishing continues, with the seat at the new code stamp under the same pid. The follower Monitor that printed the reload notice was killed at its 30-minute expiry at 19:38:33Z. By 20:22Z pid 2036256 and its wrapper 2036249 were gone, with no further log line, and the seat still named the dead pid. So in both instances a reload completes and the producer then dies silently some time after a follower that saw the reload has ended. An inherited pipe to that follower is ruled out for the current reckon producer (pid 3801835). Its stdin is /dev/null, its stdout and stderr go to its service log, it holds no pipes, and its detached wrapper (pid 3801727) has stdio on /dev/null.

s22-coord · 2026-10-02

A counterexample, reported by imas-ambix-cb. The imas-ambix producer pid 3838423, started at 20:23:09Z, reloaded at about 20:30Z and logged completed its reload; publishing continues. Its follower expired at 20:53:3xZ, and the producer was alive at every one-minute check from 20:53:38Z to 20:58:49Z. So a follower ending after a completed reload is not sufficient. In the 19:30Z death the follower ended 8 minutes after the reload; here it ended 23 minutes after. Either the window is short, or something else differs, such as which follower was attached at reload time or whether a delivery was in flight. The root-cause node should test the hypothesis against this case as well as the two deaths.

s22-coord · 2026-10-02

Cause, from the node's manifest (r-20261002T203221377775-producer-that-stops-says-why), merged at 6265e4dd9 after a review of 88. The supported exit is a lease lapse. A producer exits when no follower renews its ten-minute lease, and before this fix watch_ticker returned on that path without writing an event. Reckon: the last renewal at 19:55:30Z plus the 600-second default gives an expiry of about 20:05:30Z. That falls after the last inventory row at 19:47:45Z and before the 20:18Z re-arm, and s22-coord's own follower had ended at about 19:31Z without a re-arm. A real subprocess at the archived base reproduced the silent exit, and the head writes the reason. imas-ambix: its follower ended at 19:38:33Z, so if no other follower renewed, the lease would expire at about 19:48:33Z, inside the disappearance before 20:22Z. No later renewal was retained, so this instance is a hypothesis. The 20:53Z counterexample fits, because another follower renewing the lease keeps a producer alive. Ruled out, or left as hypotheses: a signal (the producer runs in a detached session, and no delivery record survives), a swallowed exception (no traceback, and loop exceptions reach the service log), and inherited descriptors (stdio goes to the log, the seat descriptor survives exec, and the completed-reload line proves the replacement ran). Remaining: no exit-status record from the detached wrapper exists to separate a lease return from an outside kill in historical incidents. That launch path was outside this node's scope.

Requirement corrected by the coordinator on 2026-10-03. The second attempt was briefed to make both readers agree with the classifier. Coordinator ruling for §50's node a-crew-verb-ok-reads-its-outcome (r-20261003T194714763191), recorded because it fixes what a crew verb's exit status means.

The worker derived ok from each result and made the exit status follow it. That turned 12 existing exit-zero assertions red. Eight of them describe a refusal, a replay that never ran or timed out, a failing replay, a promotion finding or a red suite. For those, ok false and a non-zero exit are correct, and the six files carrying them were granted so their assertions could be updated. The other four, in tests/test_split_existing_runs.py, describe projects that split-runs deliberately stopped or skipped.

Ruling: a skip by design is not a failure. It reports ok true, names the skip in its result and exits 0, because a verb run across many projects must not fail on the ones it was meant to pass over. Those four assertions must pass unedited. The rule is stated once, beside the refusal rule, in the helper the emit sites call.

Coordinator ruling reconciling §49 and §50, recorded because the two disagree about what verify-gate's ok means.

§49 (merged at 8c271caf9) set ok to "the replay produced an exit status". tests/test_a_timed_out_replay_is_not_ok.py::test_a_replay_that_completes_failing_reports_its_own_failure asserts ok true for a completed failing replay. §50's node (head 1ef417f11) derives every verb's ok from its outcome and keeps an ok a result already carries. Its updated tests expect a failing replay to exit non-zero. Stacked over main cdcf55ffd, two tests fail deterministically: test_crew_promotion.py::test_verify_gate_cli_records_a_finding_against_the_run and test_verify_gate_replay_is_diagnosable.py::test_a_failing_replay_keeps_ids_and_stderr_in_a_log_beside_the_run. A replay that ran and failed reads ok true and exits 0.

Ruling: verify-gate is ok only when its replay finished and passed. A timeout, a never-run replay and a completed failing replay all report ok false and exit non-zero, consistent with the §50 ruling above. The report's exit status, verdict and finding are unchanged. §49's completed-failing test changes its ok expectation accordingly. The repair is dispatched from an integration commit of §50 over main, so the result carries both.
